walkthroughs.body_html:
Ecosystems, Biodiversity & Management — a core area of GCSE Geography.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Ecosystems, Biodiversity & Management brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Ecosystems, Biodiversity & Management.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: What does Spearman's rank correlation coefficient measure?
options: The strength and direction of a relationship between two ranked variables. Values range from -1 (perfect negative) through 0 (no correlation) to +1 (perfect positive).
A Spearman value close to 1 proves that one variable causes the other.
Spearman's rank measures the average rank of all the data points.
Push factors are physical and pull factors are economic.

mcqs.q: What is the difference between push and pull factors in migration?
options: Push factors drive people away from their origin (war, poverty, persecution, disaster); pull factors attract people to a destination (jobs, safety, family, healthcare, education).
Push and pull factors are the same thing.
Push factors are physical and pull factors are economic.
A megacity has over 1 million people and a world city has over 5 million.
